items.stem: Based on the passage, which of the following is most likely to be a reason for the Constitution being called a 'living document'?
If a new law is passed that contradicts the basic structure of the Constitution, what would be the most likely outcome according to the passage?
The passage discusses how the Indian Constitution is both sacred and can be amended. How does this duality affect the way it is treated in practice?
A student argues that the Constitution should never be amended because it was created by the best people. What is the most accurate response to this argument based on the passage?

If a political party wants to amend a part of the Constitution that requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament, what is the minimum number of members that must support the amendment bill in the Lok Sabha, which has 545 members?
Which of the following is an example of a flexible part of the Indian Constitution?
According to the passage, which of the following is true about the Indian Constitution?
If a new state is to be admitted into the Union of India, which of the following procedures is followed?
The passage mentions that the Constitution was amended 106 times in 74 years. Which of the following could explain the high number of amendments?
According to the passage, which of the following is a principle of amending the Constitution in most modern countries?
The passage discusses the amendment process in the context of political history. Which of the following best explains why the Constitution was amended frequently during periods of coalition politics?
Based on the information in the passage, which of the following is NOT required for amending the Constitution of India?
According to the passage, which group of amendments includes changes that make no substantial difference to the original provisions of the Constitution?
According to the passage, what is the main reason for requiring ratification by half the State legislatures for certain amendments?
If a new amendment is made to increase the retirement age of High Court judges, which category of amendments would this fall into?
Based on the passage, why might the passage suggest that the Constitution is a 'living document'?
Which of the following best explains why the passage says that the number of amendments may not indicate that the Constitution is too flexible?
What is the main idea of the passage?
Choose the correct statement from the following.
Which of the following is not a correct statement about the amendment process of the Indian Constitution?
Which of the following is a correct statement about the Indian Constitution?
Which of the following best explains the role of the judiciary in the Indian Constitution?
According to the passage, which of the following best explains the role of the Judiciary in the Kesavananda ruling?
Which of the following best describes the idea of the Constitution as a 'living document' according to the passage?
Which of the following best explains why the 42nd Amendment was controversial?
The passage mentions that the basic structure theory was not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution. Which of the following best explains why this theory is still accepted by all institutions?

The passage describes the Constitution as a living document that adapts to societal changes. Which of the following scenarios best reflects the idea of a 'living document' as explained in the passage?
Which of the following is an example of a constitutional amendment that was later revoked due to political backlash?
The passage states that the Constitution is durable because of its ability to be dynamic and responsive to societal changes. Which of the following best supports this statement?
What does the passage suggest about the original Constitution of India?
According to the passage, which type of amendment is described as 'only a technical amendment'?
Which principle of constitutional amendment ensures that the views of the general public are considered?
What does the passage imply about the relationship between the judiciary and the Parliament in the context of constitutional amendments?
Which of the following is not a reason for making amendments to the Indian Constitution according to the passage?
Which of the following is a requirement for amending articles related to the distribution of powers between the States and the central government?
According to the passage, what is the primary principle behind the amendment procedure of the Indian Constitution?
Which amendment extended the duration of the Lok Sabha from five to six years?
Which of the following best describes the role of the judiciary in relation to the Indian Constitution?
Which of the following is a feature of a flexible constitution?
Which of the following best explains the significance of the 'basic structure' theory in the Indian Constitution?
